# How this reference app was made

Generated from the original project's own archetype (r7's pinned snapshot):

    mvn archetype:generate -DarchetypeCatalog=local \
        -DarchetypeGroupId=de.terrestris -DarchetypeArtifactId=shogun-core-webapp-archetype \
        -DarchetypeVersion=5.3.14-SNAPSHOT -DgroupId=de.example -DartifactId=shogunref \
        -Dversion=1.0 -Dpackage=de.example.shogunref -Dwebapp-name=shogunref

then patched. Nothing in shogun-core itself is changed; every behaviour the
hidden tests check is the library's.

The archetype is out of date with the library at this snapshot, so:

1. `pom.xml`: the dependency `de.terrestris:shogun-core` (the parent pom) is
   `shogun-core-main` (the jar).
2. Four generated classes had `{package}.x.Y;` instead of `import ...x.Y;` (an
   archetype template escape that no longer renders); fixed to imports.
3. `ProjectContentInitializer` and `ProjectApplicationPermissionEvaluator` used a
   `LOG` field the library no longer has; each now declares its own logger.

For r8:

4. PostgreSQL instead of H2 (Rust has no H2 driver): the
   `org.postgresql:postgresql` 42.4.3 dependency (the version the parent pom
   manages), `hikari.dataSourceClassName=org.postgresql.ds.PGSimpleDataSource`,
   `hibernate.dialect=de.terrestris.shoguncore.hibernate.ShogunPostgresqlDialect`
   (the library's own), and `jdbc.url`/`username`/`password` from `R8_JDBC_URL`,
   `R8_DB_USER`, `R8_DB_PASSWORD` (defaults: the sandbox's `aidb`, user `ai`).
5. REST security: the archetype's "demo scenario" lets ROLE_USER reach only
   `/rest/users` and keeps everything else for ROLE_ADMIN. For the slice
   (users, groups, roles, layers, layerdatasources, layerappearances) every
   user may call the endpoints and the library's entity permission evaluators
   decide, so permissions are exercised on every entity type of the slice.
6. Hibernate's second-level cache off: the Spring context set a cache region
   factory but never passed `hibernate.cache.use_second_level_cache`, so
   Hibernate's default (on) applied and entities were served from memory after
   the hidden tests had reset the database with SQL. Caching is not part of
   the contract (a port has none); with it off, every request reads the
   database.

Run (Java 8, port 8081):

    R8_JDBC_URL=jdbc:postgresql://host:5432/db mvn -DskipTests jetty:run   (add -o once its dependencies are local)

`hibernate.hbm2ddl.auto=create`: every start drops and recreates the schema
and the archetype's initial content (users admin/shogun and user/shogun,
roles ROLE_ADMIN and ROLE_USER, two groups, two OSM layers).

/usr/bin/createdb
/usr/local/cargo/bin/cargo
/usr/local/cargo/bin/rustc
/usr/bin/mvn

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<beans:beans xmlns="http://www.springframework.org/schema/security"
       xmlns:beans="http://www.springframework.org/schema/beans"
       xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
       xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.springframework.org/schema/beans
                           http://www.springframework.org/schema/beans/spring-beans.xsd
                           http://www.springframework.org/schema/security
                           http://www.springframework.org/schema/security/spring-security.xsd">
    <!-- Authentication Manager -->
    <authentication-manager alias="authenticationManager">
        <authentication-provider ref="shogunCoreAuthenticationProvider" />
    </authentication-manager>
    <beans:bean id="basicAuthEntryPoint" class="org.springframework.security.web.authentication.www.BasicAuthenticationEntryPoint">
        <beans:property name="realmName" value="SHOGun Realm" />
    </beans:bean>
    <beans:bean id="basicAuthenticationFilter" class="org.springframework.security.web.authentication.www.BasicAuthenticationFilter">
        <beans:constructor-arg ref="authenticationManager"/>
        <beans:constructor-arg ref="basicAuthEntryPoint" />
    </beans:bean>
    <!-- (Additional) Basic auth security for REST -->
    <http auto-config='false' entry-point-ref="basicAuthEntryPoint" pattern="/rest/**" use-expressions="true" access-decision-manager-ref="accessDecisionManager">
        <!-- Demo scenario: users will only get access to the /rest/users interface -->
        <!-- r8: the slice is open to every user; entity permissions decide -->
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/users/**" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/users" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/groups/**" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/groups" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/roles/**" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/roles" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/layers/**" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/layers" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/layerdatasources/**" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/layerdatasources" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/layerappearances/**" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/layerappearances" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <!-- All other interfaces can only be accessed by admins -->
        <intercept-url pattern="/**" access="hasRole('${role.superAdminRoleName}')"/>
        <custom-filter ref="basicAuthenticationFilter" before="FORM_LOGIN_FILTER"/>
        <csrf disabled="true"/>
    </http>
    <!-- Web/URL security -->
    <http auto-config="true" use-expressions="true" access-decision-manager-ref="accessDecisionManager">
        <logout logout-url="/logout" />
        <!-- As CSRF protection is enabled by default in Spring Security 4,
             the logout-url will only work with POST requests. To work with
             GET requests CSRF has to be disabled -->
        <csrf disabled="false"/>
        <!-- URL security -->
        <intercept-url pattern="/login/**" access="permitAll" />
        <intercept-url pattern="/user/register.action" access="permitAll" />
        <intercept-url pattern="/user/activate.action" access="permitAll" />
        <intercept-url pattern="/user/resetPassword.action" access="permitAll" />
        <intercept-url pattern="/user/changePassword.action" access="permitAll" />
        <intercept-url pattern="/**" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')" />
    </http>
    <!-- Enables Method Security and Expression-based access control -->
    <global-method-security pre-post-annotations="enabled">
        <!-- Enables custom expression handler -->
        <expression-handler ref="methodExpressionHandler" />
    </global-method-security>
    <!-- BEANS -->
    <!-- bcrypt password encoder -->
    <beans:bean id="bcryptEncoder" class="org.springframework.security.crypto.bcrypt.BCryptPasswordEncoder">
        <!-- Configure the strength (log rounds). Default = 10 -->
        <beans:constructor-arg value="10"/>
    </beans:bean>
    <!-- Custom Authentication Provider -->
    <beans:bean id="shogunCoreAuthenticationProvider" class="de.terrestris.shoguncore.security.ShogunCoreAuthenticationProvider">
        <beans:property name="passwordEncoder" ref="bcryptEncoder" />
    </beans:bean>
    <!-- This bean is referenced by the http security config to assure that the role hierarchy will be used -->
    <beans:bean id="accessDecisionManager" class="org.springframework.security.access.vote.AffirmativeBased">
        <beans:constructor-arg>
            <beans:bean id="webExpressionVoter" class="org.springframework.security.web.access.expression.WebExpressionVoter">
                <beans:property name = "expressionHandler">
                    <beans:bean id="webExpressionHandler" class="org.springframework.security.web.access.expression.DefaultWebSecurityExpressionHandler">
                        <beans:property name = "roleHierarchy" ref="roleHierarchy" />
                    </beans:bean>
                </beans:property>
            </beans:bean>
        </beans:constructor-arg>
    </beans:bean>
    <!-- See http://goo.gl/o42k1S -->
    <beans:bean id="methodExpressionHandler" class="org.springframework.security.access.expression.method.DefaultMethodSecurityExpressionHandler">
    <!-- To use hasPermission() in expressions, configure a PermissionEvaluator -->
         <beans:property name = "permissionEvaluator" ref="permissionEvaluator" />
         <beans:property name = "roleHierarchy" ref="roleHierarchy"/>
    </beans:bean>
    <beans:bean id="permissionEvaluator" class="de.terrestris.shoguncore.security.access.ShogunCorePermissionEvaluator">
        <beans:property name="permissionEvaluatorFactory">
            <!-- This is how project specific permission evaluators can be used/configured -->
            <beans:bean class="de.example.shogunref.security.access.factory.ProjectEntityPermissionEvaluatorFactory" />
        </beans:property>
    </beans:bean>
    <!-- http://static.springsource.org/spring-security/site/docs/3.0.x/apidocs/org/springframework/security/access/hierarchicalroles/RoleHierarchyImpl.html -->
    <beans:bean id="roleHierarchy"  class="org.springframework.security.access.hierarchicalroles.RoleHierarchyImpl">
        <beans:property name="hierarchy">
            <beans:value>
                ${role.superAdminRoleName} > ${role.defaultUserRoleName}
            </beans:value>
        </beans:property>
    </beans:bean>
</beans:beans>

content.text: The HTML error pages are noisy, so I'll switch to a helper that prints just the status and a truncated body.

input.command:
mkdir -p /tmp/probe && cat > /tmp/probe/t.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# usage: t.sh BASE [curl args...] -- prints status and truncated body
BASE=$1; shift
out=$(curl -s -w '\n__CODE__%{http_code}' "$@")
code=${out##*__CODE__}
body=${out%__CODE__*}
if echo "$body" | grep -q '<html>'; then body="(html error page)"; fi
echo "[$code] $(echo "$body" | tr -d '\n' | cut -c1-${LEN:-300})"

content.text: The probe settles several non-obvious points. Restricted listings put `id` back only when it's requested, and `output:only` on `layerdatasources` returns a 500. Nested calls inside the service bypass the security proxy, so `/groups/5/users` returns 200 `[]` rather than 404. Before I try mutations, I'll make a reset tool that restores the same seed into both databases.

input.command:
cd /tmp/probe && pg_dump -a -d ref > seed.sql 2>/dev/null; grep -c 'COPY' seed.sql; TABLES=$(psql -d ref -At -c "select string_agg(quote_ident(tablename), ', ') from pg_tables where schemaname='public'"); echo "$TABLES" | cut -c1-200; cat > reset.sh <<EOF
#!/bin/bash
# usage: reset.sh DBNAME  -- restore the seed data into DBNAME (schema must exist)
set -e
psql -q -d "\$1" -c "TRUNCATE $TABLES CASCADE" >/dev/null
psql -q -d "\$1" -f /tmp/probe/seed.sql >/dev/null
EOF
chmod +x reset.sh && ./reset.sh port && psql -d port -c 'select count(*) from users' -c 'select * from hibernate_sequences'; ./reset.sh ref && psql -d ref -c 'select count(*) from users'

content.text: The appearance PUTs confirm the behaviour: an embedded object whose id already exists, or doesn't exist, gives 404; one without an id creates a new row; `null` clears the link. Next I'll test the remaining cases: a PUT referencing an unreferenced existing appearance, POST with an existing id as a nested object, user creation with a raw password, and login for role-less or inactive users.

reset; echo "q POST layer with appearance id 14"; LEN=150 $P $R -u admin:shogun -H "$H" -X POST $R/layers -d '{"name":"x","appearance":{"id":14,"attribution":"zz"}}'; psql -d ref -At -c 'select id,attribution,opacity,visible,maxresolution from layerappearances order by id' -c 'select id,appearance_id from layers order by id'
reset; echo "r POST layer with appearance id 999"; LEN=150 $P $R -u admin:shogun -H "$H" -X POST $R/layers -d '{"name":"x","appearance":{"id":999}}'
reset; echo "s POST user raw password"; LEN=300 $P $R -u admin:shogun -H "$H" -X POST $R/users -d '{"accountName":"bob","firstName":"Bob","password":"pw1","active":true}'; psql -d ref -At -c 'select id,accountname,password,active from users order by id' -c 'select id,firstname,lastname,birthday,language,email from persons order by id'
echo "s2 login as bob"; LEN=120 $P $R -u bob:pw1 $R/users/4
reset; echo "t POST user no roles then login"; $P $R -u admin:shogun -H "$H" -X POST $R/users -d '{"accountName":"bob","password":"$2a$10$i5FKdpmNrUgYlBoS3fljY.BN//ToGs4HgleeiFbju1Ypa0TzVHWlW","active":true}'; LEN=120 $P $R -u bob:shogun $R/users; LEN=120 $P $R -u bob:shogun $R/roles
echo "t2 user with role but inactive"; reset; $P $R -u admin:shogun -H "$H" -X PUT $R/users/4 -d '{"id":4,"active":false}' ; LEN=120 $P $R -u user:shogun $R/roles

echo "v PUT group 6 roles back and user roles"; reset; $P $R -u admin:shogun -H "$H" -X PUT $R/users/4 -d '{"id":4,"roles":[]}' >/dev/null; LEN=120 $P $R -u user:shogun $R/roles

content.text: These results add several rules. A valid user with no authorities gets 401, not 403. A nested object whose id matches the layer's current appearance gets 404, while other existing ids overwrite the row. POST and PUT store passwords raw. My login test was wrong (I used the hash as the password), so I'll redo it with a real bcrypt hash, and also probe the 403 case and permission grants.

input.command:
cd /tmp/probe; P=./t.sh; R=http://localhost:8081/rest; reset(){ ./reset.sh ref; }; H='Content-Type: application/json'; ADMINHASH='$2a$10$i5FKdpmNrUgYlBoS3fljY.BN//ToGs4HgleeiFbju1Ypa0TzVHWlW';
reset; echo "w POST user w/o roles with bcrypt(shogun)"; $P $R -u admin:shogun -H "$H" -X POST $R/users -d "{\"accountName\":\"bob\",\"password\":\"$ADMINHASH\",\"active\":true}" >/dev/null; LEN=100 $P $R -u bob:shogun $R/users; LEN=100 $P $R -u bob:shogun $R/users/42
echo "x role ROLE_FOO only"; $P $R -u admin:shogun -H "$H" -X POST $R/roles -d '{"name":"ROLE_FOO","description":"foo"}'; psql -d ref -At -c 'select id,name from roles order by id'
reset; $P $R -u admin:shogun -H "$H" -X POST $R/roles -d '{"name":"ROLE_FOO","description":"foo"}' >/dev/null; $P $R -u admin:shogun -H "$H" -X POST $R/users -d "{\"accountName\":\"bob\",\"password\":\"$ADMINHASH\",\"active\":true,\"roles\":[{\"id\":43}]}"; LEN=100 $P $R -u bob:shogun $R/users; LEN=100 $P $R -u bob:shogun $R/roles/43
echo "y user with roles [{id:2}] referencing role via object"; reset; 
echo "z POST group with owner, members, roles"; reset; LEN=400 $P $R -u admin:shogun -H "$H" -X POST $R/groups -d '{"name":"G","owner":{"id":4},"members":[{"id":4},{"id":3}],"roles":[{"id":2}]}'; psql -d ref -At -c 'select * from usergroups order by id' -c 'select * from user_usergroup' -c 'select * from usergroups_roles' 
echo "z2 POST group members nonexistent"; LEN=200 $P $R -u admin:shogun -H "$H" -X POST $R/groups -d '{"name":"G","members":[{"id":999}]}'
echo "z3 POST group owner nonexistent"; LEN=200 $P $R -u admin:shogun -H "$H" -X POST $R/groups -d '{"name":"G","owner":{"id":999}}'
echo "z4 POST group with roles nonexistent"; LEN=200 $P $R -u admin:shogun -H "$H" -X POST $R/groups -d '{"name":"G","roles":[{"id":999}]}'
echo "z5 POST group members with name(ignored)"; reset; LEN=200 $P $R -u admin:shogun -H "$H" -X POST $R/groups -d '{"name":"G","members":[{"id":4,"accountName":"zzz"}]}'; psql -d ref -At -c 'select * from user_usergroup' -c 'select id,accountname from users'
echo "z6 PUT user 4 userGroups [5]"; reset; LEN=300 $P $R -u admin:shogun -H "$H" -X PUT $R/users/4 -d '{"id":4,"userGroups":[5]}'; psql -d ref -At -c 'select * from user_usergroup order by 1,2'
echo "z7 PUT user 4 userGroups []"; reset; LEN=300 $P $R -u admin:shogun -H "$H" -X PUT $R/users/4 -d '{"id":4,"userGroups":[]}'; psql -d ref -At -c 'select * from user_usergroup order by 1,2'
echo "z8 PUT group 5 members [4]"; reset; LEN=300 $P $R -u admin:shogun -H "$H" -X PUT $R/groups/5 -d '{"id":5,"members":[{"id":4}]}'; psql -d ref -At -c 'select * from user_usergroup order by 1,2'
echo "z9 PUT group 6 members []"; reset; LEN=300 $P $R -u admin:shogun -H "$H" -X PUT $R/groups/6 -d '{"id":6,"members":[]}'; psql -d ref -At -c 'select * from user_usergroup order by 1,2'
echo "z10 PUT user 4 userGroups [5,6] (both sides)"; reset; LEN=300 $P $R -u admin:shogun -H "$H" -X PUT $R/users/4 -d '{"id":4,"userGroups":[5,6]}'; psql -d ref -At -c 'select * from user_usergroup order by 1,2'
echo "z11 PUT user 4 userGroups [999]"; reset; LEN=300 $P $R -u admin:shogun -H "$H" -X PUT $R/users/4 -d '{"id":4,"userGroups":[999]}'
echo "z12 PUT group 6 owner 4"; reset; LEN=300 $P $R -u admin:shogun -H "$H" -X PUT $R/groups/6 -d '{"id":6,"owner":{"id":4}}'; psql -d ref -At -c 'select id,name,owner_id from usergroups order by id'
echo "z13 PUT group 6 owner null"; reset; LEN=300 $P $R -u admin:shogun -H "$H" -X PUT $R/groups/6 -d '{"id":6,"owner":null}'; psql -d ref -At -c 'select id,name,owner_id from usergroups order by id'
echo "z14 PUT user 4 roles [{id:1}]"; reset; LEN=300 $P $R -u admin:shogun -H "$H" -X PUT $R/users/4 -d '{"id":4,"roles":[{"id":1}]}'; psql -d ref -At -c 'select * from users_roles order by 1,2'
echo "z15 PUT user 4 password"; reset; LEN=100 $P $R -u admin:shogun -H "$H" -X PUT $R/users/4 -d '{"id":4,"password":"newpw"}'; psql -d ref -At -c 'select id,password from users order by id'
echo "z16 PUT user 4 accountName dup"; reset; LEN=100 $P $R -u admin:shogun -H "$H" -X PUT $R/users/4 -d '{"id":4,"accountName":"admin"}'
echo "z17 POST role dup name"; LEN=100 $P $R -u admin:shogun -H "$H" -X POST $R/roles -d '{"name":"ROLE_ADMIN"}'
echo "z18 POST role no name"; LEN=100 $P $R -u admin:shogun -H "$H" -X POST $R/roles -d '{"description":"x"}'
echo "z19 DELETE role 2 (used by user 4)"; reset; LEN=100 $P $R -u admin:shogun -X DELETE $R/roles/2
echo "z20 DELETE group 6 (member user 4)"; reset; LEN=100 $P $R -u admin:shogun -X DELETE $R/groups/6; psql -d ref -At -c 'select * from user_usergroup' -c 'select * from usergroups_roles' -c 'select id,name from usergroups'
echo "z21 DELETE group 5 owned by user 3 wait"; reset; LEN=100 $P $R -u admin:shogun -X DELETE $R/groups/5
echo "z22 DELETE role unused"; reset; LEN=100 $P $R -u admin:shogun -X POST $R/roles -d '{"name":"R3"}' >/dev/null; LEN=100 $P $R -u admin:shogun -X DELETE $R/roles/43

content.text: This batch shows the response-echo rule. A POST or PUT returns nested objects exactly as the client sent them (missing fields defaulted), while nested objects absent from the body are shown as loaded from the DB. The POST that listed member 3 after member 4 dropped member 3, which I think is a same-millisecond `created` collision in `equals`, not intended behaviour. Next, permission grants for a non-admin and the 403-versus-401 question.

input.command:
cd /tmp/probe; P=./t.sh; R=http://localhost:8081/rest; reset(){ ./reset.sh ref; }; H='Content-Type: application/json';
psql -d ref -At -c "select 'entity41 in: ' || (select count(*) from layers where id=41) || (select count(*) from modules where id=41) || (select count(*) from users where id=41)"
reset; echo "e1 role ROLE_FOO only user"; $P $R -u admin:shogun -H "$H" -X POST $R/roles -d '{"name":"ROLE_FOO"}' >/dev/null; $P $R -u admin:shogun -H "$H" -X POST $R/users -d '{"accountName":"bob","password":"$2a$10$i5FKdpmNrUgYlBoS3fljY.BN//ToGs4HgleeiFbju1Ypa0TzVHWlW","active":true,"roles":[{"id":42}]}'; LEN=100 $P $R -u bob:shogun $R/users; LEN=100 $P $R -u bob:shogun $R/roles/42; LEN=100 $P $R -u bob:shogun $R/roles/42 -X PUT
echo "g1 grant READ on layer 16 to user (4) via permissions"; reset; psql -q -d ref -c "insert into permissioncollections(id,created,modified) values (100,now(),now())" -c "insert into permissioncollections_permissions values (100,'READ')" -c "insert into userpermissions values (16,100,4)"
LEN=200 $P $R -u user:shogun $R/layers; LEN=200 $P $R -u user:shogun $R/layers/16; LEN=200 $P $R -u user:shogun "$R/layers?output:only=name"; LEN=200 $P $R -u user:shogun "$R/layers/filter?name=OSM-WMS%20GRAY"
echo "g2 PUT layer16 as user with READ only"; LEN=100 $P $R -u user:shogun -H "$H" -X PUT $R/layers/16 -d '{"id":16,"name":"q"}'
echo "g3 grant UPDATE too"; psql -q -d ref -c "insert into permissioncollections_permissions values (100,'UPDATE')" -c "update permissioncollections set id=100 where id=100"; LEN=100 $P $R -u user:shogun -H "$H" -X PUT $R/layers/16 -d '{"id":16,"name":"q"}'; psql -d ref -At -c 'select id,name from layers where id=16'
echo "g4 DELETE layer16 as user (no DELETE)"; LEN=100 $P $R -u user:shogun -X DELETE $R/layers/16
echo "g5 grant DELETE via group permission"; psql -q -d ref -c "insert into permissioncollections_permissions values (100,'DELETE')"; LEN=100 $P $R -u user:shogun -X DELETE $R/layers/16
echo "g6 layer 16 deleted; now test with maps: map 28 has 15 and 16?"; psql -d ref -At -c 'select * from maps_layers' -c 'select id from maps'

content.text:
I have enough of the original's behaviour to write the Rust service. My plan:

- **Stack**: axum as the HTTP layer with one fallback handler doing manual routing (so 400/401/403/404/405 ordering matches Spring), sqlx for PostgreSQL, bcrypt for passwords, serde_json for JSON.
- **Model**: in-memory structs whose fields are `Option` where the Java side can be null. Each struct has `apply` (Jackson-style partial update), `to_json`, `project` (`output:only`) and `filter` fields.
- **Persistence**: ids come from `hibernate_sequences` in autocommit, so failed writes still consume ids. Cascaded children (appearance, tile grid, grid extent) are written only when the body supplies them. The "already associated" 404 is reproduced for cascaded objects whose id is already in the entity's current graph.

I'll start with the project manifest and the model layer.

content.text: The dump script spawns several `psql` calls per table, which would make a full run very slow. I'll change it to one generated SQL script per database, run in a single session, and limit it to the tables these endpoints touch.

input.command:
cd /tmp/probe && cat > mkdump.py <<'EOF'
import subprocess
TABLES = """users persons users_roles usergroups usergroups_roles user_usergroup roles layers maps_layers maps modules
layerappearances layerappearances_properties layerdatasources imagewmslayerdatasources tilewmslayerdatasources
wfslayerdatasources wmtslayerdatasources wmtslayerdatasources_urls wmtstilegrids wmtstilegrids_matrixids tilegrids
tilegrid_resolution extents xyzlayerdatasources xyzlayerdatasrc_resolution userpermissions grouppermissions
permissioncollections permissioncollections_permissions hibernate_sequences overviewmaps_layers""".split()
def build(db):
    lines = []
    for t in TABLES:
        cols = subprocess.run(["psql", "-d", db, "-At", "-c",
            f"select string_agg(quote_ident(column_name), ',' order by ordinal_position) from information_schema.columns where table_schema='public' and table_name='{t}' and column_name not in ('created','modified')"],
            capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
        lines.append(f"select 'T {t}';")
        lines.append(f"select x from (select row_to_json(s)::text x from (select {cols} from {t}) s) q order by x;")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
if __name__ == "__main__":
    import sys
    for db in ["ref", "port"]:
        open(f"/tmp/probe/dump_{db}.sql", "w").write(build(db))
EOF
python3 mkdump.py && cat > dump.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# usage: dump.sh DB -> canonical dump of the relevant tables (timestamps excluded)
psql -d "$1" -At -f /tmp/probe/dump_$1.sql
EOF
chmod +x dump.sh; time ./dump.sh port | wc -l; ./reset.sh port; ./dump.sh port | md5sum; ./reset.sh ref; ./dump.sh ref | md5sum

184 of 205 pass. The real differences fall into five groups:

- **Non-JSON bodies**: the comparator should accept error pages from both sides, since only status matters there.
- **Nonexistent `userGroups` ids**: the original fails while deserialising (a proxy's `hashCode` throws), before any id is allocated. I'll check group references before allocating.
- **Lenient birthdays**: Joda accepts `1990-5-17`, so the parser must too.
- **Null map values**: the original accepts `{"a": null}` in the response and drops the null from the DB.
- **WMTS grid with a plain grid's id**: the original's `UPDATE wmtstilegrids` affects no row, so it fails with 404.
- **Allocation order on PUT**: the original allocates a new grid's id before the extent conflict fails.

I'll fix all of these.

input.content:
# shogun-rest

A Rust service that serves the `/rest` slice of SHOGun-Core (`users`, `groups`,
`roles`, `layers`, `layerdatasources`, `layerappearances`) on the schema that the
Java application creates. It answers the same URLs, status codes and JSON, and
writes the same rows.

## Build, run, test

    cargo build --release --locked
    DATABASE_URL=postgres://user:pass@host:5432/db PORT=8080 target/release/shogun-rest
    DATABASE_URL=postgres://user:pass@host:5432/db cargo test --release --locked

`DATABASE_URL` must point at a database with `schema.sql` loaded. The integration
tests create their own fixtures with fixed high ids and remove them again; without
`DATABASE_URL` they are skipped.

## Layout

| file | role |
|---|---|
| `src/main.rs` | configuration, pool, listener |
| `src/http.rs` | routing as Spring MVC maps it (400 for a bad id, 405 for a wrong method, 404 for unknown paths), the nested `userGroups` / `users` endpoints |
| `src/auth.rs` | HTTP Basic login: `users` table, bcrypt `$2a$` only, roles of the user and of its groups, `ROLE_ADMIN` above `ROLE_USER` |
| `src/perm.rs` | entity permissions: admin, self/member READ, READ-for-everyone entities, explicit user and group permission maps |
| `src/entity.rs` | the generic controller operations (list, filter, get, create, update, delete) and their status codes |
| `src/resources.rs` | the six resources |
| `src/model.rs` | entities, Jackson-style parsing of request bodies, JSON output, `output:only` and filter fields |
| `src/query.rs` | `output:only` and filter parsing (Java split rules, BeanUtils value conversion) |
| `src/store.rs` | SQL: loading with embedded relations, saving with Hibernate's cascades and join tables, deleting with owned rows |

## Behaviour that is reproduced on purpose

* A failed create is 400; a failed read, update or delete is 404; a list failure is 500.
* A PUT body that does not parse is 404; a missing or mismatched `id` is 400; an empty body is 400.
* Unknown properties are rejected (404 on PUT, 400 on POST); `created`, `modified` and the permission maps are accepted and ignored.
* Passwords are stored as given (not hashed), as the Java REST controller does.
* Ids come from `hibernate_sequences` (row `default`, new id = `next_val + 1`), allocated outside the request transaction, so a failed request still consumes ids.
* `output:only` on a single entity or on a filter is handled like the Java list code: restricted beans carry no permission maps, so only roles and appearances are visible to non-admins; `layerdatasources` fails with 500 when rows exist.
* A PUT that nests an object whose id is already part of the entity's current cascade graph (the current appearance, tile grid or grid extent) fails with 404.
* Nested objects in a body are echoed as sent (defaults for missing fields), while objects not in the body are shown as loaded from the database.
* Creating or setting a layer's `source` through the body, and creating a data source, are refused as in the original.

## Known gaps

* XYZ `resolutions` are stored by the original as Java-serialised bytes; they are read as an empty list, and a non-empty list in a request fails.
* `created` and `modified` are set with `now()`; list order is by id.

---
name: shogun-rest-port
description: Status of the Rust port of the SHOGun /rest slice in /work/rust, and the Java behaviours confirmed against the running reference app
metadata:
  type: project
---

Rust service in /work/rust (axum + sqlx + bcrypt). Builds with `--locked`, `cargo test` passes with and without DATABASE_URL.
Differential tests (original on :8081 with db `ref`, Rust on :8090 with db `port`, same seed) passed 315 cases in the last run.

**Why:** the port must match the Java original byte-for-byte on status, JSON and DB rows; these behaviours were confirmed on the running original, not just read from source.

**How to apply:** when changing the Rust code, re-check against the original rather than the source. Non-obvious confirmed behaviours:
- A valid user with no roles (directly or via groups) gets 401; a user with roles but neither ROLE_USER nor ROLE_ADMIN gets 403.
- Non-admin POST is always 400 (CREATE is never granted on a new entity). Non-admin PUT/DELETE of an unreadable entity is 404.
- `output:only` on a single GET is ignored; on lists, non-admins see nothing from users/groups/layers (restricted beans have no permission maps), roles and appearances stay visible. `layerdatasources` with output:only returns 500 when rows exist.
- Filters: no usable criteria gives [] (no query); invalid int gives 0, invalid boolean false (BeanUtils defaults).
- Layer delete removes the layer from maps and needs UPDATE on each such map (else 404).
- PUT with a nested object whose id is already in the entity's current cascade graph (appearance, tile grid, grid extent) gives 404; XYZ extent (no cascade) is exempt.
- Failed writes still consume ids from hibernate_sequences (table generator commits separately).
- Passwords are stored raw by the REST API; login then needs a bcrypt hash that Spring accepts ($2a$ only).
- New TileGrid defaults tileSize to 256; Java Sets collapse equal elements (dedupe members/roles).
- Properties with nested object/array values are stored as Java toString (`{a=1}`, `[1, 2]`).

Related: [[project-shogun-rest-harness]] for how the differential harness is run.

content.text:
The Rust port is in `/work/rust` and meets the goal. `cargo build --release --locked` and `cargo test --release --locked` pass, both with and without `DATABASE_URL`. The binary serves all six resources on `PORT` without any Java.

**How I checked it:** I ran the original app on port 8081 and the Rust service on 8090, each on its own database loaded from the same seed. For every case the harness resets both databases, sends the same request to each, and compares status, canonical JSON, a dump of the relevant tables (timestamps excluded), and the `hibernate_sequences` value. All 315 cases match. They cover login and role outcomes, every endpoint and nested endpoint, `output:only`, filters, nested-object semantics, permission grants, cascades, and deletes.

**Behaviour I reproduced on purpose.** These come from the original, not the spec:
- Authentication: a valid user with no roles gets 401; a user with roles but no `ROLE_USER` or `ROLE_ADMIN` gets 403.
- Create: non-admin POST is always 400, since CREATE is never granted on a new entity.
- Errors: a failed PUT, DELETE or single GET is 404; a PUT body that doesn't parse is 404, while a missing or mismatched id is 400.
- Restricted listings: `output:only` gives non-admins nothing for users, groups and layers. Data sources with `output:only` return 500 when rows exist.
- Layer delete removes the layer from its maps and needs UPDATE on each map.
- Nested objects whose id is already in the entity's current cascade graph give 404.
- Failed writes still consume ids, so id allocation commits separately.
- Passwords are stored raw by the REST API.

**Known gaps:**
- XYZ `resolutions` are read as empty, and a non-empty list in a request fails with 404. The original stores them as Java-serialised bytes, which the spec says isn't checked.
- `created` and `modified` are set with `now()`, and lists come back ordered by id. Neither is checked.
- Duplicate members in a POST are deduped by content. The original's dedupe depended on timing, and I didn't copy that accident.
- Clippy isn't installed, so there was no lint pass. The build has no warnings.

**Test suite:** the unit tests cover parsing, filter conversion and auth helpers. The integration tests run the router against `DATABASE_URL` using fixed high ids, and clean up afterwards. They were also run against a schema-only database with no data.

**Cleanup:** I stopped the original app and my service, deleted `rust/target/` and the original's `target/`, and left `Cargo.lock`, `Cargo.toml`, `README.md` and `src/` in `rust/`. The comparison databases `ref` and `port` still exist.
